exposure: duration of the 2nd stage of labour
Duration of the 2nd stage of labour
first vaginal birth after caesarean section (CS)
outcome: Rate of obstetric anal sphincter injury (OASI)
cohort: 28,535 women with their first VBAC and 275,439 nulliparous women with a vaginal delivery from the Dutch perinatal registry
finding: While women with a VBAC generally have a higher risk of OASI compared to those having their first vaginal delivery, this risk is influenced by factors like the indication for previous CS and is not increased in those with a prior CS for suspected fetal distress.
mod_finding: Women with VBAC have a higher rate of OASI compared to women with a first vaginal delivery, with the exception of women with a vaginal birth after an emergency CS for suspected fetal distress.
